findings: A well-circumscribed, pleural-based soft-tissue opacity is identified along the right lateral mid-to-upper chest wall.

The lesion forms obtuse angles with the adjacent chest wall, characteristic of an extrapleural or pleural origin (such as a localized fibrous tumor of the pleura, pleural plaque, schwannoma, or chest wall lesion).
No overt bone destruction or focal cortical disruption is visualized in the adjacent ribs.
The remainder of the right lung and the entire left lung are clear without focal consolidation, pneumothorax, or large pleural effusion.
The cardiomediastinal silhouette and bilateral hilar contours are within normal limits.
Both costophrenic angles are sharp and preserved.
